recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future broad CodeSystem text cleanup should be handled under the later issue that approves it; no additional FHIR-13291 work is needed.
issue_request: FHIR-13291 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 vocabulary change request for CodeSystem. It objected to the Scope and Usage paragraph saying CodeSystem was intended for smaller ad-hoc code systems, and asked the specification to recognize larger code system metadata use cases such as describing SNOMED filters/properties without distributing all concepts.
initial_application: Jira records svn 14618. Git commit 4760695131b6e151598f29ffc90c7f918c1e480f (GF#13291 - fix codesystem scope) changed source/codesystem/codesystem-introduction.xml by removing the smaller-ad-hoc limitation and adding the current wording about publishing properties and optionally content, plus declaring filters and properties for large code systems.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has CodeSystem as an active resource. Current source search found the old smaller-ad-hoc phrase only in source/history.html as part of a FHIR 1.4.0 Connectathon historical change note, not current CodeSystem resource guidance. Later CodeSystem-related issues found during checking, including FHIR-54129 and FHIR-36644, concern separate text corrections or filter patterns and do not reverse the FHIR-13291 scope change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current CodeSystem Scope and Usage text already reflects the issue resolution, and changing the historical release-note occurrence would not improve current CodeSystem semantics.
